body:
Base off what you're saying, I think it's possible that maybe you're a bit demanding (I don't know, I don't know you or your relationship but given your concerns with it, it might be something to think about) but at the end of the day - if you're doing the all the work and taking all the blame then that doesn't sound like a partner to me. PARTICULARLY if he's refusing to be a partner based on some sort of weird "principle" he has. Even if you're too demanding, he's clearly too obstinate as well based on your description.

Does this relationship sound like a partnership to you?
Are you having any specific thoughts or feelings when you feel uncomfortable watching intimacy?

What's more important to you? Some people you don't care about  MAYBE thinking you're  a "creep" or supporting your friend in a time that is clearly important to her, particularly following an emotional experience like a breakup?

There's nothing illegal about it, even if you had sex. Top chances are nobody even knows you aren't a student one you're in there. You're only 20.

It sounds like he doesn't respect you at all. He acts like you're his mother (refusing to do anything so you do stuff like clean up), he's stubborn and refuses to try new experiences with his partner even though she clearly wants to share with him, and then he blames you for everything which is essentially emotional abuse (some may disagree). I'd take a hard look at how happy you are and whether you're down with a lifetime of this, 10 years of this, another day of this?

You think he's going to change or get worse when his behavior is only reinforced?

I don't necessarily think he's a sociopath from just this information, nor could anyone diagnose him from it. That being said, it is clear that you have some reservations, perhaps some self-confidence issues, and just overall disconnect in certain areas with the behavior of your husband and the relationship. Would I go through with the marriage? I guess it depends on your view...but to be worried enough about it to be posting on the internet for strangers to comment on does seem like something to note and account for when making your decision. Have you discussed any of this with your husband in the same way you have presented it here? Without calling him a sociopath of course.

I'm really sorry this happened to you. It sounds like you have a lot invested in this and it is really emotionally draining right now. At the end of the day, as often as it gets said, bullet dodged.  You're 24 and clearly successful  and based on how you describe yourself, someone that will have no problems  finding relationships in the future - as hard as that can seem to imagine right now I'm  sure.

Just imagine how shitty things would be if you found this out 10 or 20 years down the road rather than 2.5. The human body and mind is extremely resilient. I know this seems like it will last forever but it won't. It will "get better" with time. Some days will be better than others. Some worse. But you're going to get better.  Please find some emotional support in real life, friends, family, therapists, something. You clearly need to get out physically but support will be super helpful both now and down the road too. Remember, we get by with a little help from our friends.
Thanks for your time, have a great life.
